# Background

Cancer treatment is frequently associated with adverse effects on physical function, psychological well-being, and quality of life. Resistance exercise has emerged as an effective strategy to mitigate many of these consequences. However, access to supervised exercise programmes remains limited for many patients.

Digital exercise interventions may increase accessibility and flexibility while maintaining many of the benefits of traditional on-site exercise programmes. The purpose of this report is to compare a digital home-based resistance exercise programme with a supervised on-site programme using a simulated dataset.

# Methods

## Data

The repository contains three datasets:

- `participants.csv`
- `measurements.csv`
- `training_diary.csv`

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)

participants <- read_csv("data/participants.csv")
measurements <- read_csv("data/measurements.csv")
training_diary <- read_csv("data/training_diary.csv")

measurements <- measurements %>%
  mutate(
    test = factor(test, levels = c("pre", "post"))
    )
```

## Exercise Adherence

```{r}
adherence_summary <-

  training_diary %>%
  group_by(fp) %>%
  summarise(
    adherence_sets =
      mean(sets_completed / sets_max),

    adherence_reps =
      mean(reps_completed / reps_max),

    adherence =
      mean(c(adherence_sets,
             adherence_reps)),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    participants %>%
      select(fp, group),
    by = "fp"
  )
```

# Results

# Participant Characteristics

## Table 1. Baseline Characteristics

```{r}
table1 <-

  participants %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Age_mean = round(mean(age),1),
    Age_sd = round(sd(age),1),
    Males = sum(sex=="male"),
    Females = sum(sex=="female")
  )

table1
```

# Exercise Adherence

## Figure 1. Exercise Adherence by Group

```{r}
ggplot(
  adherence_summary,
  aes(group, adherence, fill = group)
) +
  geom_violin(alpha = .5) +
  geom_boxplot(width = .15) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Adherence",
    title = "Exercise Adherence by Group"
  )
```

## Adherence Comparison

```{r}
t.test(
  adherence ~ group,
  data = adherence_summary
)
```

# Physical Performance Outcomes

## Prepare Data

```{r}
change_scores <-

  measurements %>%

  select(
    fp,
    test_name,
    test,
    test_value
  ) %>%

  pivot_wider(
    names_from = test,
    values_from = test_value
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    delta = post - pre
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    participants %>%
      select(fp, group),
    by = "fp"
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    adherence_summary %>%
      select(fp, adherence),
    by = "fp"
  )
```

# Push-Up Performance

## Figure 2. Pre-Post Changes in Push-Ups

```{r}
pushups <-

  measurements %>%
  filter(test_name == "push-ups") %>%
  left_join(
    participants %>%
      select(fp, group),
    by = "fp"
  )

ggplot(
  pushups,
  aes(
    x = test,
    y = test_value,
    group = fp,
    colour = group
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = .15) +
  stat_summary(
    aes(group = group),
    fun = mean,
    geom = "line",
    linewidth = 2
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

## Mixed Model

```{r}
pushup_model <-

  lmer(
    test_value ~ group * test +
      (1|fp),
    data = pushups
  )

anova(pushup_model)
```

# Leg Press Strength

## Figure 3. Change Scores

```{r}
change_scores %>%
  filter(test_name == "legpress") %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      group,
      delta,
      fill = group
    )
  ) +
  geom_violin(alpha = .5) +
  geom_boxplot(width = .15) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    title = "Change in Leg Press Strength",
    y = "Change Score"
  )
```

# Mental Health

## Figure 4. PHQ-9 Pre-Post Changes

```{r}
phq <-

  measurements %>%
  filter(test_name == "phq-9") %>%
  left_join(
    participants %>%
      select(fp, group),
    by = "fp"
  )

ggplot(
  phq,
  aes(
    test,
    test_value,
    group = fp,
    colour = group
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = .15) +
  stat_summary(
    aes(group = group),
    fun = mean,
    geom = "line",
    linewidth = 2
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

# Adherence-Response Relationship

## Figure 5. Adherence versus Improvement in Push-Ups

```{r}
pushup_change <-

  change_scores %>%
  filter(test_name == "push-ups")

ggplot(
  pushup_change,
  aes(
    adherence,
    delta
  )
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = "Adherence",
    y = "Improvement in Push-Ups"
  )
```

## Linear Regression

```{r}
summary(
  lm(
    delta ~ adherence,
    data = pushup_change
  )
)
```

# Dropout Analysis

## Figure 6. Age Distribution by Dropout Status

```{r}
ggplot(
  participants,
  aes(
    age,
    fill = dropout
  )
) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 15,
    alpha = .7,
    position = "identity"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

## Logistic Regression

```{r}
dropout_model <-

  glm(
    dropout_bin ~ age + sex + group,
    data = participants,
    family = binomial
  )

summary(dropout_model)
```

# Outcome Summary

```{r}
change_scores %>%
  group_by(
    test_name,
    group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean_Change = round(mean(delta),2),
    SD_Change = round(sd(delta),2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

# Discussion

Participants in both groups improved on most outcomes over time. Adherence was high in both groups, with slightly higher adherence in the on-site group. Improvements in physical performance tended to be associated with better adherence.

These findings support the feasibility of both exercise delivery formats and illustrate how reproducible workflows can be implemented using Git, GitHub, Quarto, and R.
